name: feature-voting

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows the first row in its voted state with the trigger filled white, plus the full list.

tagline: Rows of feature requests with a clickable upvote counter.
summary: A list of requested features, each with a small up-arrow button and a live vote count. Clicking the arrow adds your vote and highlights the button; clicking again takes it back.
appearance: A bold white heading, Vote for Features, above four stacked rows on a dark panel. Each rounded outlined bar holds a small square upvote button at left with a triangle and a number, then a white feature title and a faint grey description.
behaviour: Clicking a row's upvote button adds one to its count, fills the button white and marks the vote pressed; clicking again lowers the count and clears the fill. An optional group can reorder rows by vote total.
demo_content: Vote for Features heading and rows for Dark Mode, API Integrations, Mobile App and PDF Export.
use_when: Users should prioritise a backlog or wishlist by casting one vote each on the ideas they want.
avoid_when: There is no per-user persistence out of the box, and long descriptions make the rows tall on mobile.
customise: Root takes value or defaultValue, votedFeatures or defaultVotedFeatures, onValueChange and disabled; Group sorts by votes-asc, votes-desc or none. Labels and layout come from your own child elements.
weight_why: A handful of list rows and a small React context; no animation loop.

a11y.note: Triggers are real buttons with aria-pressed and a changing label, and the list itself is labelled; no reduced motion is needed.

issues: Description text is very low contrast on the dark rows.
polish_why: Clear hierarchy and tidy rows; descriptions sit low contrast against the dark panel.
